answers: Another fatality in the Boston bombings has been identified: The family of 29-year-old Krystle Campbell says she was killed as she and a friend were cheering on another friend who was racing, reports WCVB. "This is just a waste," says her mother. “Everyone that knew her loved her. She was always smiling. You couldn’t ask for a better daughter. She was the best.” Campbell was a restaurant manager, reports the Boston Herald, which notes an especially wrenching detail: Her father was initially told she was alive, but when he got to the ICU, he realized it was his daughter's friend who had survived. Campbell is the second of the three people killed to be identified. The first was 8-year-old Martin Richard, and his father, Bill, released a statement today thanking supporters and asking for privacy, reports WBZ. "My dear son Martin has died from injuries sustained in the attack on Boston. My wife and daughter are both recovering from serious injuries. We thank our family and friends, those we know and those we have never met, for their thoughts and prayers. I ask that you continue to pray for my family as we remember Martin. We also ask for your patience and for privacy as we work to simultaneously grieve and recover. Thank you." The third victim was a grad student at Boston University, but the person's identity is being withheld until the family says it's OK to release, reports USA Today.

**Summary of Boston Marathon Bombings News**

On April 15, 2013, two bombs exploded near the finish line of the Boston Marathon, resulting in tragic casualties and widespread shock across the city. Among the victims was 8-year-old Martin Richard from Dorchester, who was killed in the attack. His mother, Denise, and his 7-year-old sister were seriously injured and are recovering in local hospitals. Martin was at the race to watch his father, Bill Richard, a community leader in Dorchester. A vigil was held in his honor at Garvey Park, where neighbors and strangers came together to offer support and condolences. The Richard family has requested privacy as they grieve and recover.

Another victim was Krystle Campbell, a 29-year-old restaurant manager from Medford. Her family was initially misled by hospital staff, who told them she had survived the attack, only to later discover that she had died. Campbell was at the finish line to cheer on a friend who was running. Her father described her as a caring and loving person, and her mother expressed deep grief and disbelief at the tragedy.

The third identified victim was a Chinese graduate student from Boston University, who was watching the race with two friends near the finish line. The student's name and gender were not released pending family approval, and relatives requested that the student not be identified. One of the student's friends was injured but in stable condition.

In response to the bombings, FBI officials stated there were no known additional threats and vowed to find those responsible. Mayor Thomas Menino emphasized the city's strength and determination to heal and move forward. Enhanced security measures were implemented at public transportation hubs and airports, and the city worked to restore normalcy as quickly as possible.

The tragedy brought out a wave of national and international solidarity. President Obama praised the resilience and compassion of the American people, while Pope Francis expressed deep sorrow and called for unity against evil. The city also saw acts of kindness, such as the Salvation Army providing food and emotional support, and runners and residents coming together to support one another.

The bombings left a lasting impact on the community, with many still struggling to process the loss and trauma. Despite the pain, Boston showed a strong spirit of unity and resilience, determined to recover and rebuild.
